page: Microsoft Azure NV12ads_V710_v5 is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine belonging to the NVadsV710v5 series, tailored for graphics workloads and visual processing. Powered by an AMD x86_64 processor, the instance provisions 12 dedicated vCPUs managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The compute resources are paired with 64 GB of system memory, establishing an allocation of 5.33 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Hardware acceleration on the NV12ads_V710_v5 is supplied by an AMD V710 GPU partition, providing a 0.5 fractional GPU allocation with 12 GB of dedicated video memory. This fractional structure allows virtualized environments to access hardware-based graphics pipelines without provisioning an entire physical GPU die. Fast temporary storage is bundled directly on the host, consisting of an 825 GB NVMe SSD with Azure Premium Storage capability.

The fractional GPU model yields operational cost efficiency for deployments where graphical tasks do not demand a full dedicated accelerator. By pairing 12 dedicated compute cores and 64 GB of host memory with half of an AMD V710 processor, the platform balances host-side data handling with visual compute. A primary tradeoff involves scalability limits, as workloads requiring extensive multi-GPU parallelization or unpartitioned hardware access may encounter throughput limits on this instance tier.

Given its specific resource distribution, the NV12ads_V710_v5 is structured for virtual desktop infrastructure, interactive 3D modeling, computer-aided design, video encoding, and entry-to-midrange graphics rendering tasks.
